The region $D$ in the right-half plane is enclosed between two semi-circles centered at $O$ of radii $1$ and $4,$ as shown above. What is 
${∬}_{D}\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A$
expressed in polar coordinates?
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form 

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

The region $D$ represents a portion of the washer enclosed between the circles of radii $1$ and $4$ centered at the origin. In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(r,\theta )\,:\,1\le r\le 4,\,-\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{Δ}\frac{r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{{r}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }{{r}^{2}({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{1}^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$
